$comment: The judgement calls — everything that cannot be extracted from code. Props, tokens, tests and adoption are generated; this file holds what a human decided. Keep it honest: it is what the inventory site and AGENTS.md publish.
summary: Choose one of a known set of options. A form control first: it posts a value.
description: Select covers single-choice fields with roughly 4–15 known options — country, role, sort order. It wraps the primitive layer's Select, so typeahead, wheel and touch scrolling, focus return and aria-activedescendant management are inherited, not owned. The trigger uses the same field anatomy as TextField and the popup uses the same overlay surface as Dialog, so a form full of mixed controls reads as one system.
useFor: Choosing exactly one of 4–15 known options: country, timezone, role, sort order
Form fields that post a value — `name` wires the hidden input for a plain form submit
Grouped option sets (`Select.Group` with a label) where the categories aid scanning
dontUseFor: 3 or fewer options — RadioGroup shows them all in one glance for the same cost; a select hides them behind a click
More than ~15 options, or options loaded async — that scrolling-and-hunting interaction is what Combobox exists to replace
Actions that fire on selection ('Export as…') — that is Menu's contract; a Select that navigates or mutates on change breaks every user who cursors through options to hear them
Multi-select — this component's value is a single string by design; a multi-select is a different control with different announcement semantics

keyboard.action: On the closed trigger: opens, focus moves to the selected (or first) item
Open: moves the highlight; does not wrap silently past the ends
Open: jumps to the first / last item
Open AND closed: jumps to the next matching option — closed-state typeahead selects without opening
Open: selects the highlighted item, closes, returns focus to the trigger
Open: closes without selecting, returns focus to the trigger
Open: closes and moves focus on (the primitive's default — deliberately not overridden)

provides: A visible label wired to the trigger — `label` is required by the prop types, so an unlabelled select cannot compile
The primitive's full combobox/listbox semantics: typeahead, focus return to the trigger on every close path, aria-activedescendant management
description and error joined into one aria-describedby chain, in reading order
`aria-invalid` plus role="alert" on the error text, so an appearing error is announced rather than discovered on the next focus
Form participation via a hidden input when `name` is set — a plain <form> post includes the value
A reserved indicator column, so labels do not shift when the selection changes
consumerMustProvide: A label that names the FIELD ('Country'), not the instruction ('Choose one')
Error text that says what to do, paired with the border colour — never colour alone
Stable, unique `value` strings on items; the value is what posts, the children are what humans read
limitations: Options render into the DOM when open, so a very long list costs real layout time — beyond ~15 options reach for Combobox, which virtualises and filters
axe passes cannot tell you the option ORDER makes sense or that the label is useful; that stays a human review

doDont.dont: Use it for 3 or fewer — use RadioGroup
doDont.why: Radios show every option in one glance for the same screen cost; a select hides them behind a click and a scan. Below four options you are adding interaction cost and removing information.

doDont.do: Reach for Combobox when options exceed ~15 or arrive async
doDont.dont: Add a filter input inside the Select popup
doDont.why: Scrolling a Select of 200 items is the interaction Combobox exists to replace. A filter input bolted inside a Select is Combobox built badly: the focus model, typeahead and announcement semantics all fight each other.

doDont.do: Keep the trigger showing the selected value
doDont.dont: Use a Select as an action menu ('Export as…' that fires on selection)
doDont.why: That is Menu's contract. Screen-reader and keyboard users cursor through options to hear them read; a Select that navigates or mutates on change executes an action per arrow-key press.

doDont.do: Pair `error` with text — it joins the aria-describedby chain and announces via role="alert"
doDont.dont: Signal invalid by border colour alone
doDont.why: 3:1 contrast on a 1px border is not a message. Colour-blind users, zoomed-in users and screen-reader users all need the words; the red border is the accent, not the content.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Compound items, not an options array — so an item can grow an icon or a disabled state without the API changing.
examples.code:
<Select label="Country" placeholder="Select a country" name="country">
  <Select.Item value="au">Australia</Select.Item>
  <Select.Item value="nz">New Zealand</Select.Item>
  <Select.Item value="jp">Japan</Select.Item>
  <Select.Item value="de">Germany</Select.Item>
</Select>

examples.title: Description and error
examples.description: Both join the trigger's aria-describedby chain, description first. The error also sets aria-invalid and announces on appearance.
examples.code:
<Select
  label="Shipping region"
  description="Determines available carriers."
  error="Select a region to continue."
>
  <Select.Item value="apac">Asia–Pacific</Select.Item>
  <Select.Item value="emea">EMEA</Select.Item>
</Select>

examples.title: Groups
examples.description: Group labels aid scanning and are announced with the group.
examples.code:
<Select label="Instrument">
  <Select.Group label="Strings">
    <Select.Item value="violin">Violin</Select.Item>
    <Select.Item value="cello">Cello</Select.Item>
  </Select.Group>
  <Select.Separator />
  <Select.Group label="Brass">
    <Select.Item value="trumpet">Trumpet</Select.Item>
  </Select.Group>
</Select>

examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: value + onValueChange pass straight through to the primitive — the wrapper holds no mirrored state, so a frozen parent freezes the displayed value too.
examples.code:
const [sort, setSort] = useState('newest');

<Select label="Sort by" value={sort} onValueChange={setSort} size="sm">
  <Select.Item value="newest">Newest first</Select.Item>
  <Select.Item value="oldest">Oldest first</Select.Item>
</Select>
